title: Cantaloop (Flip Fantasia)
composer: Herbie Hancock, Rahsaan Kelly, Geoff Wilkinson, Mel Simpson
original_issue: Blue Note (single, October 1992; also on the LP Hand On the Torch, November 1993)
personnel: Us3 (Geoff Wilkinson and Mel Simpson, producers); Rahsaan Kelly (rap); Gerard Presencer (trumpet); the album credits also list Dennis Rollins (trombone), Mike Smith and Ed Jones (saxophones), Tony Remy (guitar) and Matt Cooper (piano), not assigned by track in the source
trivia: A London group signed to Blue Note built this record on a sample of Herbie Hancock's tune Cantaloupe Island, with live trumpet from Gerard Presencer over the loop. It reached No. 9 on the US Hot 100 in 1993 even though it did not chart in the UK on first release.

track.title: Cantaloop (Flip Fantasia)

The album page lists 4:39 for the album track and the single page 4:41; 4:41 is used. Writers are the Wikipedia infobox list. Tagged crossover: a jazz-rap pop hit rather than a jazz-musician record.

title: Rebirth of Slick (Cool Like Dat)
composer: Ishmael Butler, Craig Irving, Mariana Vieira
original_issue: Pendulum/Elektra (single, 9 Nov 1992; also on the LP Reachin' (A New Refutation of Time and Space), 9 Feb 1993)
personnel: Ishmael Butler, Craig Irving and Mariana Vieira (raps); contains a sample of Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers' Stretching
trivia: The trio's debut single laid relaxed rhymes over a loop from Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers, and Cleveland.com later called it the pinnacle of jazz rap. It peaked at No. 15 on the US Hot 100 in March 1993, topped the Hot Rap Singles chart and won the Grammy for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group.

track.title: Rebirth of Slick (Cool Like Dat)

The personnel line is the rap trio only, since the source does not credit sidemen. Tagged crossover: a hip-hop single built on a jazz sample, not a jazz-musician record.

artist: The Brand New Heavies feat. N'Dea Davenport
title: Never Stop
composer: The Brand New Heavies (individual writing credits not verified)
original_issue: FFRR (single, 23 Sep 1991, David Morales remix; the song was added to the 1991 reissue of the LP The Brand New Heavies)
personnel: N'Dea Davenport (vocals), Jan Kincaid (drums, keyboards), Andrew Levy (bass, keyboards), Simon Bartholomew (guitar), Jim Wellman (tenor and soprano saxophones, keyboards), Lascelles Gordon (percussion, guitar); David Morales (remix)
trivia: The London acid-jazz band's first crossover hit paired its funk groove with the voice of American singer N'Dea Davenport, who joined in 1991. The David Morales remix reached No. 43 in the UK and No. 54 on the US Hot 100, and its drum beat was sampled for George Michael's 1992 hit Too Funky.

track.artist: The Brand New Heavies feat. N'Dea Davenport

Neither page names the songwriters, so the composer field names the band only. The personnel line is the 1991 band line-up from the album page, not credited by track. Acid jazz sits on the funk edge of jazz, so this is a borderline jazz card.

title: Always There
composer: Ronnie Laws, William Jeffrey, Paul B. Allen III
original_issue: Talkin' Loud/Mercury (single, 17 Jun 1991; also on the LP Inside Life, 1991)
personnel: Jean-Paul 'Bluey' Maunick (guitar, producer, band leader), Jocelyn Brown (lead vocals); the other players are not credited in the sources used
trivia: Incognito turned a 1975 Ronnie Laws tune, by way of the 1976 Side Effect vocal version, into their breakthrough hit, and bandleader Bluey Maunick said bringing in Jocelyn Brown was Gilles Peterson's idea. It reached No. 6 in the UK and No. 2 in the Netherlands, where only Bryan Adams kept it off the top.

A second version of the tune already in the set (Ronnie Laws, 1975). It was also No. 8 in Belgium, but the band is British, so no region tag. The personnel line names only the two credited artists.

title: For Sephora
original_issue: Polydor (album Live at the North Sea Jazz Festival '92, 14 Jun 1993)
personnel: Stochelo Rosenberg (lead guitar); Nous'che Rosenberg (rhythm guitar); Nonnie Rosenberg (double bass)
trivia: Stochelo Rosenberg wrote this tune as a tribute to his sister Sephora, and it has become a cornerstone of modern gypsy jazz. It opens the trio's live album from the North Sea Jazz Festival in The Hague, recorded on 12 July 1992 when Stochelo was 24.

track.title: For Sephora
track.album: Live at the North Sea Jazz Festival '92
track.query: Rosenberg Trio For Sephora Live at the North Sea Jazz Festival 92 1992
track.notes: live version (4:28, track 1)

notes: The recording date (12 July 1992, North Sea Jazz Festival, The Hague) and the release date (14 June 1993) come from AllMusic's album page as quoted in search results; AllMusic itself could not be opened, so confidence is medium. MusicBrainz confirms the 1993 Polydor release, the track order and the 4:28 length, and a German library record gives catalogue 519 466-2 and names Stochelo as composer; Wikipedia lists the album as Verve/Polydor. The studio version is on Gipsy Summer (1991) but no recording date was found for it, so the dated live version is used; the query may return the studio take, one year earlier. Tier C: a signature tune for gypsy jazz fans rather than a general-audience name, though a Samois performance with Bireli Lagrene has about 2.9 million YouTube views. One of two Rosenberg Trio cards, with Caravan.

title: Caravan
original_issue: Verve and Polydor (album Caravan, 1994)
personnel: Stochelo Rosenberg (lead guitar); Nous'che Rosenberg (rhythm guitar); Nonnie Rosenberg (double bass). The violinist Stephane Grappelli is credited as a guest on the album, but the sources do not say which tracks he plays
trivia: Caravan was written by Juan Tizol, with Duke Ellington credited as co-composer and Irving Mills as lyricist, and the Rosenberg Trio plays it as gypsy swing on the album named after it. The sessions ran from 18 January to 3 February 1994 in Paris and Hilversum, and the violinist Stephane Grappelli, whom the trio had accompanied on tour, is a guest on the record.

Release year 1994 is given by MusicBrainz, Wikipedia and Gallistrings; AllMusic and one other discography list 1993, which does not fit the 1994 sessions. MusicBrainz credits the work to Ellington and Tizol and lists this track at about 2:59. Tier B: the tune is a jazz standard and the trio's uploads of it have roughly 220,000 to 310,000 YouTube views. One of two Rosenberg Trio cards, with For Sephora.
